vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: load-balancer
Version: 2.0.0

The load-balancer skill is a local configuration management tool that allows users to define load balancer pools and backend servers, storing data in a local JSONL file (~/.load-balancer/data.jsonl). The script (scripts/script.sh) uses Python to perform CRUD operations, generate Nginx/HAProxy configuration exports, and run simulated health checks and traffic distribution tests. There is no evidence of data exfiltration, malicious execution, or unauthorized network activity; the health and stats functions are purely mathematical simulations.

llm.summary: The skill appears coherent with its stated load-balancer purpose (it is a local CLI that stores data under ~/.load-balancer), but a included script file is only partially shown in the review and there are minor metadata inconsistencies — review the full script before installing.

dimensions.detail: Name, description, SKILL.md, and the script all describe local management of load balancer configs and backend servers. The requested artifacts (no external binaries or credentials) match the described purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions are limited to running scripts/script.sh and operating on a single local data file (~/.load-balancer/data.jsonl). There are no instructions to read unrelated system files, access network endpoints, or exfiltrate data.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

However the supplied script output in the review was truncated (the stats handler and remainder were omitted). Because the full script contents were not presented, the possibility that the remainder contains unexpected behavior cannot be ruled out. Review the full scripts/script.sh file (all 22,548 bytes) before installing.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism

llm.guidance: This skill appears to be a simple local CLI for managing load‑balancer configs and backend servers and stores its state in ~/.load-balancer/data.jsonl. Before installing or running it: 1) Inspect the full scripts/script.sh file (the review output showed the file truncated) to confirm there are no hidden network calls, exec/eval of downloaded code, or reads/writes to unexpected paths; 2) Note it will create and persist data in your home directory — do not add sensitive credentials or secrets to entries you store; 3) Verify you trust the upstream repository and consider running the script in a sandbox/container first; 4) The registry metadata shows version 2.0.0 while the script and SKILL.md declare 1.0.0 — treat that as a minor anomaly and double-check the actual package contents on the source repo. If you can paste the full scripts/script.sh (complete file), I can re-evaluate with higher confidence.
